assistant:
At **20:00 on 6 January**, Bus_29 was at **0.943 p.u.**, below the **0.950 p.u.** limit. The main driver was rising demand:

- Demand at Bus_29 rose from **10.56 to 11.52 MW**, accounting for **62.0%** of the voltage fall from the last within-limit reference at 18:30.
- Demand elsewhere rose by **24.68 MW** in total, accounting for another **37.9%**. The largest named contributors included Bus_28, Bus_23, Bus_25, Bus_20 and Bus_6.
- Changes in the five units’ output/set-points were **ruled out as a material cause**: they accounted for just **0.2%** of the change.

The 18:30 reference was already close to the limit at **0.952 p.u.**, so these shares explain the final deterioration into violation, not why the bus was near its limit beforehand. The main cause—local demand at Bus_29—also held when compared with a more comfortable reference and with the previous day.

This was recurrent in the measurements: Bus_29 had **12 undervoltage episodes** during the week, and demand was the main cause in all **10** episodes investigated. The 6 January episode lasted from **18:45 to 20:45**; the worst value was **0.932 p.u.** at 19:15. A warning appeared at 18:30, 15 minutes before the episode began.

A tested single-time corrective action was: “To clear Bus_29, raise the voltage set-point of Gen_bus7 from 1.000 to 1.014 p.u. Checked by a power flow: Bus_29 at 0.951 p.u., Gen_bus7 at 39.5 Mvar (range -15 to 60), no new violation.” However, holding that change from the warning through the episode did **not** keep Bus_29 within limits throughout; it also caused a violation on the Bus_5–Bus_7 line. So that snapshot fix was not sufficient as an episode-long action.

Whether weather, calendar effects, or a particular customer drove the demand rise was not tested; those would require matched weather, schedule, or customer-level metering data. Whether Bus_29 was near voltage collapse was also not tested; that needs a voltage-stability margin study.

The demand results use the default **0.95 lagging power factor** to infer reactive demand from measured active demand.
